construction_markdown: No new leaderboard code is claimed. The optimized family is as follows. Let `F=F_2[α]/(α^16+α^5+α^3+α^2+1)`, let `A=span_F2{1,α,…,α^14}`, and encode `z=Σ_{i=0}^{15}z_iα^i` by the affine truth table `H(z)_y=z_0+Σ_{i=1}^{15}z_i y_i`, indexed by `y∈F_2^15`. For `1≤h≤64` and an arbitrary binary subspace `W≤F^(65-h)`, define `M_{h,W}` to contain every polynomial `Σ_{j=0}^{65}a_jX^j` with `a_0,…,a_h` unrestricted and `(a_{h+1},…,a_65)∈W`. Evaluation on `A`, followed blockwise by `H`, gives a deterministic binary linear code of length `|A|·2^15=2^30` and dimension `16(h+1)+dim_F2(W)`. The theorem below proves that every target-qualified member has dimension at most 1040. This subsumes the upstream top-three family, obtained at `h=62`.

Consequently, for every scale `c≠0`, some `v∈V*` makes `cX(L+v)` vanish at exactly 65 points of `A` while never taking value 1 elsewhere. This fixed-scale avoidance lemma is reusable independently of the coefficient-space application.

proof_markdown:
# Prefix-free degree-65 extractor obstruction

## 1. Fixed field and inner map

Let `p(Z)=Z^16+Z^5+Z^3+Z^2+1`. Repeated squaring modulo `p` gives `Z^(2^8)=Z^8+Z^7+Z^3+Z` and `Z^(2^16)=Z`. Put `r=Z^8+Z^7+Z^3`. Exact Euclidean division gives

`p=(Z^8+Z^7+Z^6+Z^5+Z^4+Z^2+1)r+(Z^2+1)`,

`r=(Z^6+Z^5+Z^4+Z^3+Z^2+1)(Z^2+1)+1`.

Thus `gcd(p,Z^256-Z)=1`, while `p` divides `Z^65536-Z`. Rabin's degree-16 criterion proves that `p` is irreducible. Hence `F=F_2[α]/(p)` is the stated field.

Let `A=span_F2{1,α,…,α^14}`. For `z=Σz_iα^i`, define `H(z)_y=z_0+Σ_{i=1}^{15}z_i y_i`, with `y∈F_2^15`. This is binary-linear and injective. Its weights are exactly `0` at `z=0`, `32768` at `z=1`, and `16384` otherwise: in the last case a nonzero linear part makes the truth table balanced.

## 2. Subspace and inverse-span certificate

Put `U=span_F2{1,α,…,α^5}`. Starting with `L_0=X`, the recursion `β_i=L_i(α^i)`, `L_{i+1}=L_i^2+β_iL_i` has

`(β_0,…,β_5)=(0001,0006,0168,47be,b444,4c35)`

and produces

`L(X)=X^64+2e0cX^32+71eeX^16+d9a4X^8+2198X^4+c6caX^2+6115X`.

It is additive and has precisely the 64 elements of `U` as roots. Therefore `V=L(A)` has dimension `15-6=9`. A basis, obtained by evaluating at `α^6,…,α^14`, is

`e9f1,d1b4,e1cf,9bc6,ea9c,7d5e,f733,26c1,770d`.

Relative to this basis, masks `001,002,…,00f,012` give the sixteen elements

`e9f1,d1b4,3845,e1cf,083e,307b,d98a,9bc6,7237,4a72,a383,7a09,93f8,abbd,424c,3b28`.

Their respective inverses are

`073e,bd8c,866d,49ad,4923,6e3d,a335,aceb,84c4,2a71,0d54,e7eb,d1e4,f0b7,e05c,5852`.

Each paired product reduces to `0001` modulo `0x1002d`. Exact high-bit XOR elimination on the inverse words gives pivot rows

`0001,0003,0004,000b,0018,0023,0061,008e,0160,02c8,073e,0d16,1c71,3be1,49ad,bd8c`,

whose leading bits are respectively 0 through 15. They are independent, proving `span_F2(V^{-1})=F`.

## 3. Fixed-scale avoidance

For `v∈V*`, define

`S_v={0}∪{x∈A:L(x)=v}`,  `G_v(X)=X(L(X)+v)`.

Every nonzero fiber of `L:A→V` has 64 points, so `|S_v|=65`; these are exactly the roots of the monic degree-65 polynomial

`G_v=X^65+2e0cX^33+71eeX^17+d9a4X^9+2198X^5+c6caX^3+6115X^2+vX`.

In particular its `X^64` and `X^63` coefficients vanish, equivalently `e_1(S_v)=e_2(S_v)=0`.

Fix `c∈F*`. Suppose, contrary to the claim, that for every one of the 511 choices `v∈V*` there were an `x∈A` satisfying `cx(L(x)+v)=1`. Write `w=(cx)^(-1)`. Then `w∈V*` and `v=L(x)+w`. A fixed `x` determines at most one `v`, so covering all 511 values requires 511 distinct `x`; inversion then gives 511 distinct `w`, necessarily all of `V*`. Therefore `c^(-1)V^(-1)⊆A`. Taking binary spans and using the inverse-span certificate gives `F⊆A`, contradicting `dim A=15`. Thus some `v∈V*` satisfies `cG_v(x)≠1` for every `x∈A\S_v`.

## 4. Coefficient-space intersection

For `1≤h≤64` and binary `W≤F^(65-h)`, let

`M_{h,W}={Σ_{j=0}^{65}a_jX^j : a_0,…,a_h∈F, (a_{h+1},…,a_65)∈W}`.

This is binary-linear. Evaluation is injective because a nonzero degree-at-most-65 polynomial cannot vanish on all 32,768 points of `A`; blockwise `H` is injective as well. Hence

`k=dim C_{h,W}=16(h+1)+dim W`.

Let `π_h` retain coefficients of degrees `h+1,…,65` and set `T_h={π_h(cXL):c∈F}`. Its degree-65 coefficient is `c`, so `dim T_h=16`. Since the ambient suffix space has dimension `16(65-h)`, Grassmann's inequality gives

`dim(W∩T_h)≥dim W+16-16(65-h)=k-1040`.

If `k≥1041`, choose `c≠0` with `π_h(cXL)∈W`. Choose `v` from the fixed-scale lemma. The polynomial `f=cX(L+v)` has the selected suffix, while its only `v`-dependent coefficient is the degree-one term `cvX`, which is unrestricted because `h≥1`. Thus `f∈M_{h,W}`.

The word `C(f)` has 65 zero blocks, no all-one block, and 32,703 balanced blocks. Consequently

`wt C(f)=32703·16384=535,805,952<535,822,336`.

This contradicts the target. Therefore every target-qualified `C_{h,W}` has `k≤1040`.

## 5. Arbitrary standard-split two-fiber maps

Let `B_s:F_2^K→F_2^16`, `1≤s≤32768`, be arbitrary binary-linear maps, and let `e_0=(1,0,…,0)`. Define

`Δ(x)=Σ_s(1_{B_sx=0}-1_{B_sx=e_0})`.

Affine truth-table descent meets the target exactly when `Δ(x)≤64` for every `x≠0`.

For a subspace `Q≤F_2^K` of dimension `q`, put `r_s=rank(B_s|Q)`. The zero fiber of `B_s|Q` has size `2^(q-r_s)`. Its `e_0` fiber is either empty or a coset of the same size. Hence the exact identity

`Σ_{x∈Q}Δ(x)=Σ_{s:e_0∉B_s(Q)}2^(q-r_s)`.

All right-hand summands are nonnegative. Since `Δ(0)=32768` and every other member contributes at most 64,

`Σ_{x∈Q}Δ(x)≤32768+64(2^q-1)=64·2^q+32704`.

If `t(Q)` maps kill all of `Q`, their contributions alone are `t(Q)2^q`; hence `(t(Q)-64)2^q≤32704`.

Take any 65-set `T` of seeds and `Q=∩_{s∈T}ker B_s`. Then `t(Q)≥65`, so `2^q≤32704<2^15` and `q≤14`. Rank-nullity gives

`q≥K-Σ_{s∈T}rank B_s`,

therefore `K≤14+Σ_{s∈T}rank B_s≤1054`.

Writing `δ_s=16-rank B_s`, every 65-set satisfies `Σ_{s∈T}δ_s≤1054-K`. If `K≥1041`, the right side is at most 13. If total deficiency were at least 14, enough deficient seeds could be selected and the set padded to size 65, contradicting this inequality. Thus `Σ_sδ_s≤13`. At `K=1054`, every map is surjective and every 65-fold joint map has rank 1040 and common-kernel dimension 14.

## 6. Exact condenser pruning

For homogeneous maps `A_s:F_2^K→F_2^m` with `L=2^d` seeds, let `z(x)=|{s:A_sx=0}|`. Every min-entropy-one distribution is a convex combination of uniform two-point distributions. For a pair with difference `x`, exactly `z(x)` seeds merge its two atoms; each merger contributes `1/(2L)` statistical distance from the atom cap `1/(2L)`. Therefore the optimal strong entropy-one lossless-condenser error is exactly `max_{x≠0}z(x)/(2L)`.

Thus error `2^-10` is equivalent to `z(x)≤L/512`, and the maps form an additive `q=2^m` code of block distance at least `L-L/512`. Singleton gives `K≤m(2^(d-9)+1)` when `d≥9`. The elementary q-ary Plotkin double count closes the small-alphabet cases; at equality it gives size at most `qL`. Substituting `d+m=30` leaves only homogeneous splits `(16,14)` through `(20,10)` whose cap can exceed 1040, with the listed caps. At `(15,15)`, the homogeneous core cap is 975, or 976 after adjoining the all-one word.

For affine lossless maps with `m+1` output bits, the same argument replaces `m` by `m+1`. At `(15,15)` the cap is exactly `16·65=1040`; the only larger-cap splits are `(16,14)` through `(21,9)`. Consequently a standard-split `K≥1041` family must exploit the negative `z_1` term rather than merely satisfy a lossless-condenser zero-fiber bound.

These are finite obstructions and parameter reductions, not a new code construction.

proof_steps.proof: The displayed Frobenius residues and Euclidean divisions prove irreducibility. Direct pairing of affine truth tables proves the exact weights 0, 32,768, and 16,384.
proof_steps.statement: The fixed 16-bit field and affine truth-table encoder are deterministic and have the asserted spectrum.

proof_steps.proof: The subspace-polynomial recursion gives `L` and the nine-dimensional image `V`. Sixteen explicitly listed elements of `V` have the listed inverses; exact XOR elimination has pivots in all sixteen bit positions.
If all 511 nonzero fibers were covered at a fixed scale, uniqueness in `v=L(x)+(cx)^(-1)` would force `c^(-1)V^(-1)⊆A`, contradicting the inverse-span certificate and `dim A=15`.
proof_steps.statement: For every `c≠0`, some 65-root polynomial `cX(L+v)` avoids the symbol 1 at every nonroot evaluation point.

proof_steps.proof: The message space is the direct product of `h+1` unrestricted field coefficients and `W`. Degree 65 is below `|A|`, and both evaluation and `H` are injective.
proof_steps.statement: `C_{h,W}` is binary-linear of length `2^30` and dimension `16(h+1)+dim W`.

proof_steps.proof: The projected sparse space `T_h` has dimension 16 because its leading coefficient is the scale `c`. Grassmann's inequality gives `dim(W∩T_h)≥k-1040`.
proof_steps.statement: Every member with `k≥1041` contains the high-degree portion of a nonzero scaled `XL`.

proof_steps.proof: The varying term `cvX` lies in the unrestricted prefix. The resulting polynomial has exactly 65 roots and no value 1 elsewhere, producing 32,703 balanced blocks and exact weight 535,805,952.
proof_steps.statement: Every `k≥1041` prefix-free family violates the required distance.

proof_steps.proof: Summing zero-minus-`e_0` fiber counts over a subspace gives the exact nonnegative rank formula. Applying the one-sided target inequality bounds every common kernel of 65 maps by dimension 14.
Writing ranks as `16-δ_s` gives a deficiency sum at most `1054-K` on every 65-set. Integrality and padding show the same upper bound globally when `K≥1041`.
proof_steps.statement: Arbitrary standard-split two-fiber families have `K≤1054`; above 1040 their total rank deficiency is at most 13.

proof_steps.proof: Extreme points of the min-entropy-one source polytope are uniform pairs, giving exact error `max z/(2L)`. Singleton and q-ary Plotkin then yield the enumerated finite split windows.
proof_steps.statement: Ordinary entropy-one lossless-condensing cannot give `K≥1041` at the standard split, and only the listed alternative splits remain numerically open.

theorem_statement: For every `1≤h≤64` and every binary subspace `W≤F^(65-h)`, the fixed affine-inner evaluation code `C_{h,W}` formed from degree-at-most-65 polynomials with unrestricted coefficients in degrees `0,…,h` satisfies: if `d_min(C_{h,W})≥535,822,336`, then `dim C_{h,W}≤1040`. The bound is tight within this family. Independently, every arbitrary standard-split affine two-fiber family satisfying the target has dimension at most 1054, and a putative dimension at least 1041 forces total seed-map rank deficiency at most 13.
